title: Routines in one picture: charters and people
bridge: A routine is like a GitHub Action that wakes on an event or a schedule. Except: what wakes up is Nova, with the same harness, VM, walls and review layers. Its rules live in a reviewed YAML file, the charter, not in a prompt.
intro: Routines are the night crew: a CI fixer for red main, upgrade fixers for broken updates, bug fixers, and code-health sweepers. Each one is Nova with a different trigger and a charter. This lesson closes the old n8n flow, writes the first charter, loads it with zod, and names the people.

picture.caption: A routine is Nova started by an event instead of a person, held by a charter and owned by a person.

nodes.label: trigger: red main, Renovate PR, Bug, schedule

steps.text: one run per root cause starts routineRun
loads the charter pinned to an ai-agents commit
claims a VM; the harness gets the goal, done list, skills, model and paths
Edit or Write outside allowed_paths is denied; the push is checked again
is written as Requested-by: on every PR, so the owner's approval never counts
one person from the rotation, not the owner, gives the one approval

p: Nova starts when a person assigns a ticket. A routine starts when something happens: main goes red, a Renovate PR fails, a Bug is triaged, or a schedule fires. Then it runs the same harness, in the same kind of fresh VM, behind the same walls.

The difference is written down in a charter: one YAML file per routine in RhinoHealth/ai-agents. It names the owner, the trigger, the allowed paths, the never-list, the skills, the model, the VM size and what done means.

Every routine starts in shadow: it runs on real triggers and opens nothing. It moves up the trust ladder to drafts, then normal, only by a reviewed PR (lesson g5-3). One run per root cause, and no time or turn limits.

callout.text: Routines do not fork Nova. Same harness, same VMs, same walls, same review layers. Only the trigger and the charter differ, so safety is built once.

p: RH-7207 is an n8n story for a Jira-to-PR agent flow. Nova and the routines replace it. Two bots that turn tickets into PRs would confuse people and double the security work.

Spend 15 minutes with Nave, its assignee: what the n8n flow already does and what is worth keeping. Copy useful notes (Jira fields it read, prompts, failure cases) into the Jira poller ticket and G5-13.

In n8n, check that no Jira-to-PR or Claude Code workflow is active. Deactivate it; do not delete it. Comment on RH-7207 with the reason and the plan link, and close it as Won't Do. n8n stays for business flows such as Vanil.

sections.h: The charter, part 1: who, when and on what
p: The first routine is fe-ci-fixer: when frontend CI fails on main, fix it. Part 1 of its charter says who owns it, what wakes it, and what it runs on.
Two keys come back in later lessons. run_id names one run per root cause (lesson g5-2). gather_minutes waits so that failures with the same cause join one run (lesson g5-4).
sections.because: A charter turns "Nova with a different trigger" into something concrete that people can review in a PR.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/charters/fe-ci-fixer.yaml: sketch; one file per routine, loaded by routineRun (G5-08)
name: fe-ci-fixer
team: fe
owner: from people.yaml              # never approves this routine's PRs (Requested-by: line, G5-07)
stage: shadow                        # shadow → drafts → normal (G5-15); promotions only by PR
trigger:
  kind: github.workflow_run
  repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
  workflows: ["[FRONTEND] - CI"]
  branch: main
  conclusion: failure
run_id: "cifix:fcp:{fingerprint}"    # one run per root cause (G5-09)
gather_minutes: 7                    # wait, then group (G5-17)
queue: cifix                         # task queue ai-agents-cifix; 2 VM slots (G3-25)
vm: { size: lite, spot: true }       # full when the failed job needs FCP Lab (jobs.yaml, G5-20)
model: { name: claude-opus-5-5, effort: low, on_failed_checks: medium }

notes.text: One file per routine. routineRun (lesson g5-2) loads it.
The name matches the file name. The loader checks it.
The owner's GitHub handle comes from config/people.yaml. The owner never approves this routine's PRs.
Every routine starts in shadow. Promotion happens only through a PR that changes this line.
The trigger: a GitHub Actions run finished. The next lines narrow it to frontend CI failing on main.
The workflow ID pattern: one run per root cause, through the fingerprint (lesson g5-2).
Wait 7 minutes so more failures with the same cause join the run (lesson g5-4).
The task queue ai-agents-cifix, with 2 VM slots (G3-25).
A lite Spot VM. Spot is cheaper spare capacity that AWS may take back.
Opus 5.5 at low effort; a step whose checks failed re-runs at medium.

sections.h: The charter, part 2: paths, never, skills and done
p: Part 2 is the wall and the goal. allowed_paths and denied_paths say where the routine may write. The never-list adds rules on top of the false-heal check every routine gets (lesson g5-5).
At most 6 skills: more crowd the agent's context. done is the list the Stop hook asks for before the agent may say it is finished.
sections.because: Paths are a wall, so they live in the charter, the hooks and the broker, never only in a prompt.

code.text:
allowed_paths: ["frontend/**"]       # PreToolUse hook, and again in the broker's git proxy at push
denied_paths: [".github/**", "frontend/biome.json", "frontend/tsconfig.json", "frontend/playwright.config.ts"]
never: [edit_test_assertions]        # on top of the false heals every routine is checked for (G5-14)
skills: [fix-ci, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story]   # 5 of at most 6
done:
  - the failed job's commands fail on the red commit and pass on the fix, in the VM
  - npm run verify is green
  - no test weakened (false-heal check clean)
pr:
  title: "[FE] {jira}: fix red main: {summary}"
  labels: ["routine:fe-ci-fixer"]
  jira: create                       # a ticket is created or linked for every routine PR

notes.text: The routine may edit only under frontend/. A hook checks it, and the broker's git proxy checks it again at push.
Inside frontend/, still never: workflows, the lint, type and Playwright config. These are G0's locked checks.
A CI fixer may not change an existing test assertion.
The skills from G8 the session loads. 5 of at most 6.
What the Stop hook checks before "done": reproduced and fixed in the VM, verify green, no test weakened.
fcp's PR title style, with the Jira key so add-jira-links works.
The routine:<name> label. The noise rules count PRs by it (lesson g5-3).
A Jira ticket is created or linked for every routine PR.

sections.h: The Charter schema: strict on purpose
p: The schema lives in the shared package, so the orchestrator, the harness and CI read charters the same way. The ticket gives the rules, not the code; this sketch follows them.

z.strictObject rejects any unknown key. A typo like gather_minuts, or a key nobody implements like max_turns, fails the load instead of being ignored. Optional keys cover routines outside fcp: repo, read_only and setup (the kb-ingest charter uses them), plus hand_off and bump_cmd (the upgrade fixers).
sections.because: A strict schema turns a silent mistake in a charter into a red CI check on the charter's PR.

code.text:
// ai-agents/shared/src/schemas.ts (Charter; a sketch built from G5-06's steps)
import { z } from "zod";
const Effort = z.enum(["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"]);
export const Charter = z.strictObject({  // strict: an unknown key is an error, not ignored
  name: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/),
  team: z.enum(["fe", "be", "devops"]).optional(),
  owner: z.string().optional(),  // the real handle lives in config/people.yaml (G5-07)
  stage: z.enum(["shadow", "drafts", "normal"]),
  trigger: z.looseObject({ kind: z.enum(["github.workflow_run", "jira", "schedule"]) }),
  run_id: z.string().optional(), gather_minutes: z.number().int().min(0).optional(),
  queue: z.enum(["cifix", "upgrade", "flaky", "bugfix", "health", "security"]).optional(),
  vm: z.strictObject({ size: z.enum(["lite", "full", "wide"]), spot: z.boolean().optional() }),
  model: z.strictObject({ name: z.string(), effort: Effort, on_failed_checks: Effort.optional() }),
  allowed_paths: z.array(z.string()).min(1),  // empty would mean "nowhere": a mistake, so reject it
  denied_paths: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
  never: z.array(z.enum(["edit_test_assertions", "add_code", "add_retries_or_sleeps"])).default([]),
  skills: z.array(z.string()).min(1).max(6),  // more than 6 skills crowd the context
  done: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  pr: z.looseObject({ labels: z.array(z.string()) }).optional(),
  repo: z.string().default("RhinoHealth/fcp"), read_only: z.array(z.string()).optional(), setup: z.string().optional(),
  hand_off: z.array(z.looseObject({ to: z.string() })).optional(), bump_cmd: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),
});
export type Charter = z.infer<typeof Charter>;

notes.text: Strict: an unknown key is an error, not ignored.
Names are kebab-case, like the file names.
Optional here, because the owner's handle lives in people.yaml (G5-07).
The three trust-ladder stages.
Each trigger kind has its own fields, so the trigger keeps unknown keys. Only kind is checked.
VM size from G3 (lite, full, wide) and Spot or not.
An empty list would mean "nowhere", which is always a mistake.
The three charter rules the false-heal check knows (lesson g5-5).
At least one skill, at most 6.
Missing repo means fcp. zod fills the default.
The upgrade fixers' keys (lesson g5-6): packages to hand to a team, and bump commands per folder.
The TypeScript type comes from the schema: one definition.

callout.text: Because owner and team are optional, a charter without them still loads. Two do: be-upgrade-fixer has no owner (lesson g5-6), and kb-ingest has no team or queue (lesson g6-5). Add a test that every charter gets an owner from people.yaml and a queue. Also decide whether hand_off and bump_cmd stay; check which tickets use them.

sections.h: The loader, pinned to a commit
p: parseCharter reads YAML text into a Charter or throws with every problem and its key path. loadCharters reads a whole folder; a node:test test loads every charter in CI.

In the orchestrator, loading happens in an activity, loadCharter(name, sha), pinned to the ai-agents commit. Workflow code must be deterministic, and a Temporal replay must see the same charter, so the file is read at one commit.
sections.because: Reading a file is I/O, which a workflow may not do. Pinning the commit keeps a replayed run on the same rules.

notes.text: The yaml package parses the file into plain objects.
Our own error type, so a test can tell a bad charter from any other failure.
Parse the YAML, then check it. safeParse returns a result instead of throwing.
zod 4's readable error: one line per problem, with the key path.
fe-ci-fixer.yaml must say name: fe-ci-fixer, so the file name is the routine's name.
Every .yaml file in the folder, sorted, into a map by name.

sections.h: Paths are a wall: the hook and the push
p: The harness passes allowed_paths, denied_paths and never to the session. G3's blockProtectedPaths hook is extended with the charter. An Edit or Write outside the allowed paths gets a calm deny, and the PR lists the refusal.

Bash can write files the hook never sees. So the broker's git proxy checks every changed path against the same charter at git push. That is the real wall; the hook gives the early, readable refusal. Ask the broker owner (G3) to add it.
Default paths per team: FE gets frontend/**. BE gets cloud/**, client/** and sdk/**, with **/migrations/** denied in the pilot. DevOps gets the infrastructure and gitops repos plus .github/**.
sections.because: The same pathAllowed rule runs in the hook and at push, so the early refusal and the real wall never disagree.

notes.text: node:path's glob matcher: frontend/** matches any file under frontend/. Check its stability note in the Node 24 docs.
The checkout in the VM. Paths are compared relative to it.
Inside an allowed glob and not inside a denied one. The git proxy reuses this rule.
A function that builds the hook for one charter. Registered on PreToolUse with matcher Edit|Write.
Edit and Write carry file_path. Bash does not, which is why the push check exists.
Turn an absolute or ../ path into one relative to the repo before matching.
Refuse the call. The agent sees the reason and carries on with something else.

sections.h: People: owners and the reviewer of the day
p: A routine needs a person who answers for it: the owner. The owner is written as Requested-by on every PR of the routine, so G0's independent-approval check refuses the owner's approval. No new check is needed.

Each team names a reviewer rotation. When a PR is marked ready in stage normal, the orchestrator picks rotation[workingDayIndex % rotation.length]. It skips the owner and requests that one person. No CODEOWNERS file, no team-wide request.

The guilds also agree how a Bug counts as triaged into a team. Today it is mixed (labels, title prefixes, components, the Team field). The proposal is a FE or BE label on a Bug in To Do. Swaps for holidays are a one-line PR to people.yaml.
sections.because: One approval from someone who did not ask for the change is already a GitHub wall; we only name the people.

code.text:
# ai-agents/config/people.yaml (teams block): sketch. Each guild fills its own block; the handles are placeholders.
teams:
  fe:
    channel: "<FE guild Slack channel>"          # daily digest (G5-03)
    reviewers: ["<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>"]   # one per working day, Sun–Thu, in order
  be:
    channel: "<BE guild Slack channel>"
    reviewers: ["<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>"]
  devops:
    channel: "<DevOps Slack channel>"
    reviewers: ["<gh-handle>", "<gh-handle>"]
owners:                                           # written as Requested-by: on every PR of the routine,
  fe-ci-fixer: "<gh-handle>"                      # so the owner's approval never counts (G0 check)
  fe-upgrade-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  fe-bug-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  fe-dead-code: "<gh-handle>"
  be-ci-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  be-upgrade-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  be-bug-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  be-flaky-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  pipeline-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
  infra-upgrade-fixer: "<gh-handle>"
triage:                                           # how a Bug counts as triaged into a team (G5-13)
  fe: { labels: ["FE"] }                          # proposal: today labels, title prefixes and the Team field are mixed
  be: { labels: ["BE"] }

notes.text: One file for all people data. The same file maps Slack ID, Jira accountId and GitHub login (G4-05).
Where the team's daily digest goes (lesson g5-3).
The rotation: one per working day, Sunday to Thursday, in order.
One owner per routine. Written as Requested-by on every PR of that routine.
The first routine's owner, a person on the FE guild.
How a Bug counts as triaged into a team. G5-13's bug poll uses it.
The proposal: the FE label on a Bug in To Do.

callout.text: The routine owner never approves its routine's PRs. Exactly one approval counts, from the reviewer of the day or another person who is not the owner.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a routine and Nova?

options.text: A routine has its own simpler harness, so it is cheaper
options.why: Routines must not fork Nova: same harness, VMs, walls and review layers.

options.text: Only the trigger and the charter; everything else is shared
options.why: That is why safety is built once and every routine inherits it.

options.text: A routine may merge its own PRs once it reaches normal
options.why: Agents never merge. Normal only means clean PRs are marked ready for the reviewer of the day.

quiz.q: A charter has the key max_turns: 50. What happens?

options.why: z.strictObject rejects unknown keys. Ignoring them would hide typos too.
No turn limits exist on agents, and the key is not part of the schema.

options.text: Loading fails with Unrecognized key, and the charter's PR gets a red check
options.why: The CI test loads every charter, so the mistake never reaches a run.

quiz.q: The fe-ci-fixer agent runs sed -i on .github/workflows/frontend-ci.yaml through Bash. What stops the change?

options.why: The hook sees Edit and Write calls with a file_path. A Bash sed is invisible to it.

options.text: The broker's git proxy, which checks every changed path against the charter at push
options.why: That is the real wall; the hook is the early, readable refusal.
The push carries the change, and the git proxy refuses paths outside the charter.

One reviewed YAML file per routine: owner, trigger, paths, never-list, skills, model, VM and done.
The person who answers for a routine; written as Requested-by on its PRs, so never its approver.
One person from a team's rotation, never the owner, requested when a routine PR is ready.
Extra rules in a charter, such as edit_test_assertions, that the false-heal check enforces.
